_doc: Construction states of the field works for app/src/structures/works3d.mjs. The TIMES come only from the state engine (src/structures/state.mjs: the port of tools/bt/check_structures.py state_at over structures/works_stages.json and structures/state_schedule.json, gate Q08); this file adds no time except the two labelled conventions below. The FOOTPRINTS are plausible-procedural: no work of the record has a mapped line in the repository (only a named place with its sigma), so each is drawn as a contour-following line of the printed or assumed length anchored at the gazetteer place, marked plausible-procedural and shown with the place's sigma. The PROFILES are drawn only from the sourced description (PDF B.7.4: log close-fence with stone and earth, about 5 ft high, Culp's Hill: tier inferred) or from labelled assumptions (plausible-procedural); nothing is taken from the modern lidar surface of Culp's Hill or Little Round Top or from the rebuilt walls (PDF B.7.6, works_stages.json modern_profile_rule). No source was opened by this workstream.

params.segment_run_basis: PDF B.7.4: 'each segment (roughly one regiment front or a fixed run of yards)'; 40 m is a fixed run chosen here (tuning value, plausible-procedural)
params.front_basis: plausible-procedural: the length of one regiment's front in the line of works (no figure is printed; a regiment of 400 in two ranks covers about 100 m)
params.offset_basis: PDF B.7.4 assumption 2: each segment starts within a seeded offset of the work's start so the line does not rise in lockstep; the offset is at most half the window and every segment still ends at the work's finish (so none starts before the documented start)
params.stage_height_basis: PDF B.7.4 stage table: 1 layout (marks only), 2 felling and gathering (stones, logs and cordwood moved), 3 stacking (log fence, earth thrown behind), 4 head logs laid, 5 completed full height, 6 damaged (splintered head logs, scattered stone); the fractions of the full height are plausible-procedural (the PDF prints no per-stage height)
params.unresolved_basis: A window with no clock (a date only, or only a bound on the start) cannot place a segment inside the build: it is shown half-built for the whole printed window and marked uncertain, as the buildings with a date-only change are (DEC-016 (2)); the end of the window is the only instant the engine reports as complete
params.thickness_basis: plausible-procedural (PDF B.7.4 labelled assumption 3: 'the notes give no thickness'); NOT measured from the modern works
params.crew_basis: plausible-procedural: the stand-in crew of a 40 m run; the documented figure is the 12 tools of the 6th Wisconsin (B.7.4), used as the cap for E-02
params.stand_in_label: stand-in crew (builder unknown or not on the field in this layer): plausible-procedural
params.contour_basis: plausible-procedural: a breastwork on a slope follows the contour; the line is traced from the place along the horizontal of the (modern) ground and carries the place's sigma

afternoon.basis: 'afternoon' begins at noon (the meaning of the word); applied only where the record prints the part of day and no earliest clock

evening.basis: the labelled convention of src/history/placement.mjs PERIODS (evening = dusk = 19:32), owner may replace

E-01.length_basis: PDF B.7.2 E-01: about 600 yd long (Wikipedia first day: weak, so inferred)
E-01.height_basis: PDF B.7.4 assumption 4: height and rail layout are assumptions; 1.2 m (4 ft) is a stand-in for stacked fence rails
E-01.builder_text: I Corps remnants under Wainwright's artillery; no crew list printed

E-02.length_basis: one regiment front (6th Wisconsin): the rest of Wadsworth's division is named without a front
E-02.height_basis: PDF B.7.4 stage 5: about 5 ft (Culp's Hill), the only height figure found; the profile (log close-fence with stone and earth) is the sourced description
E-02.builder_text: 6th Wisconsin (Dawes), then the rest of Wadsworth's division

E-03.length_basis: one regiment front (123rd NY); the location text says lower hill: placed downhill of the upper works (the distance is a procedural stand-in)
E-03.height_basis: PDF B.7.4 Culp's Hill group, about 5 ft

or_morning_jul2.label: the 123rd NY's own report puts the breastwork on the morning of 2 July, not 1 July (shard fence-1, E-03 / S-015); the window is the date only

E-04.length_basis: the record calls it 'fortification (vague)': one front as a stand-in
E-04.builder_text: Von Steinwehr's division and two batteries; Howard left infantry and artillery

E-05.length_basis: PDF B.7.2/B.7.4: about 300 yd at first (GD-219), single thin line of about 800 yd after 18:30 (E-09); weak keys, so inferred
E-05.height_basis: PDF B.7.4 stage 5: about 5 ft; log close-fence with stone and earth

damage.basis: state_schedule S-050 and works_stages E-05 damage_stage (derived window, inferred)

E-06.length_basis: one run: a traverse is short (no length printed)

E-07.length_basis: three regiment fronts (Kane's 29th, 109th, 111th PA) of 80 m: assumption
E-07.height_basis: PDF B.7.4 Culp's Hill group, about 5 ft
E-07.builder_text: Kane's 2nd Brigade (Greene's right) and Wadsworth's I Corps men (Greene's left)

E-08.length_basis: three regiment fronts of 80 m: assumption (Lockwood's position unconfirmed)
E-08.height_basis: PDF B.7.4 Culp's Hill group, about 5 ft
E-08.builder_text: Williams's division, XII Corps (including Lockwood's brigade, position unconfirmed)

E-09.length_basis: 800 yd total (PDF S-041, GD-219) minus the first 300 yd = 500 yd: arithmetic on weak keys, so inferred
E-09.height_basis: PDF B.7.4 Culp's Hill group; 'single thin line': thinner than the first 300 yd, drawn at the same height
E-09.builder_text: Greene's brigade alone (plus about 750 reinforcements from I and XI Corps later)

damage.basis: state_schedule S-050 object list names E-09 (damaged by shelling); window as E-05

E-12.length_basis: four lunettes of 30 m (one for each battery the record names: Wiedrich, Ricketts, Stewart, Battery L 1st NY): assumption; the lunette plan is not in the repository, so each is a straight run
E-12.height_basis: no height in the record; the OR describes 'a small earthwork thrown up in its front' for each gun (shard terrain-1, G-03)
E-12.builder_text: Union batteries; builders unnamed (inference); labelled stand-in crew, builder unknown (PDF B.7.1)

or_small_earthworks_jul1_evening.label: the Official Records put a small earthwork in front of each gun at dusk on 1 July, not lunettes by 16:00 on 2 July (shards fence-1 EG-06 and terrain-1 EG-03); the window is the date only, no clock is invented

E-14.length_basis: three regiment fronts of 80 m: assumption; NOT the rebuilt Little Round Top works
E-14.height_basis: no height in the record; a stand-in low stone breastwork; NOT derived from the modern rehabilitation reconstruction (B.7.6)
E-14.builder_text: Weed's brigade, five Pennsylvania Reserve regiments, an Ohio battery (the OR names Fisher's brigade on the morning of 3 July: conflict carried, register fence-1/terrain-2)

not_drawn.E-10: occupation of the empty lower-hill works by Steuart, not a construction (state_schedule S-042); the works are those of E-03/E-08 and stay as they are
not_drawn.E-11: the shelling damage of Culp's Hill (stage 6): applied to E-05 and E-09 through their damage windows, not a work of its own
not_drawn.E-13: no construction attributed (natural ledges and boulders)
not_drawn.E-15: improvised hand-hauled gun position (S-038): unlimbered guns on natural ground, no earth
not_drawn.E-16: no works at Devil's Den (Ward lacked time or inclination)
not_drawn.E-17: open gap in the PDF: the OR documents rail breastworks on Cemetery Ridge (shard fence-1, EG-08) but gives no dimensions, continuity or start times; nothing is drawn, and rail piles are not animated as documented
not_drawn.E-18: open gap: no Confederate works found for 2-3 July
not_drawn.G-03: drawn as E-12 (the same prepared lunettes, row S-026)
not_drawn.G-12: prepared in line (Cushing's battery): the PDF rule says built on screen, but no schedule row or work record prints a window for it and no OR report mentions an earthwork (shard terrain-1, EG-12): not drawn, open gap, never pre-placed
not_drawn.G-11: improvised (McGilvery's line); the OR mentions a slight earthwork (shard terrain-1, EG-11): carried in the register, not drawn
not_drawn.G-18: the seed says no works; the OR documents earthworks at Stevens' battery (shard terrain-2, EG-11 / G-18): carried in the register, not drawn

gun_emplacement_rule.improvised: improvised position: no earth is built (PDF B.7.5 engine rules and works_stages gun_emplacement_engine_rules): guns unlimbered on natural ground
gun_emplacement_rule.no_works_described: no works described: open-ground battery position, logged as a gap (never a pre-placed pit)
gun_emplacement_rule.not_described: no works described: open-ground battery position, logged as a gap
gun_emplacement_rule.open_positions: positions not given: nothing drawn, logged as a gap
gun_emplacement_rule.mixed: mixed (Hunt's ridge line): the record gives no work; nothing drawn
